title: Gemini Decisions API: Fast, calibrated multimodal decisions

quotes.text: Today, we’re introducing the Gemini Decisions API, a new endpoint for fast, closed-set decisions powered by our new Gemini Decision 1 model (gemini-decision-1), available through the Gemini API in Google AI Studio.
quotes.for: Launch, model name and identifier, availability in Google AI Studio.

quotes.text: You can pass one multimodal input across text, images, audio, video, and PDFs (up to 256K tokens) along with up to 1,000 independent questions.
quotes.for: Input size, modalities and number of questions per request.

quotes.text: Selects from 2 to 255 choices, returning the winner and normalized probabilities for every candidate.
quotes.for: Multiple choice among 2 to 255 options, with probabilities.

quotes.text: Every answer includes a confidence score (from 0 to 1) so your code can route ambiguous cases to a fallback or human reviewer
quotes.for: Confidence score on every answer and its purpose.

quotes.text: Gemini Decision 1 is priced at $0.10 per 1M input tokens and $0 for output tokens, with an API no-cost tier you can use in Google AI Studio for prototyping.
quotes.for: Price and no-cost tier.

quotes.text: Your shared input is billed once per request no matter how many questions you evaluate
quotes.for: Shared input billed once per request.

quotes.text: With zero output tokens billed, Gemini Decision 1 with the Decisions API is nearly 5x cheaper across the shared benchmark suite than Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite with the Interactions API.
quotes.for: Cost comparison with Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite.

quotes.text: keeping median latency 50-100 ms of model compute (150-250 ms end-to-end), across multimodal inputs and contexts up to 16K tokens, remaining nearly flat from 1 to 100 questions per request
quotes.for: Latency figures and the conditions they were measured in.

quotes.text: Gemini Decision 1 leads across the suite, with the lowest calibration error.
quotes.for: Google's benchmark claim.

quotes.text: Ecosystem integrations are rolling out across OpenRouter, LangChain, Vercel, LiteLLM, Pydantic AI, Pipecat, LiveKit, and OpenCode alongside the google-genai SDKs, with support coming soon to Gemini in Google Cloud.
quotes.for: Integrations and Google Cloud support.

quotes.text: Gemini Notebook uses the Decisions API as a real-time router to instantly direct incoming queries to the optimal model tier and thinking level for each request.
quotes.for: Internal use for model routing in Gemini Notebook.

title: Google enters decision model market with Gemini Decisions API

quotes.text: A cybersecurity team, for example, could ask the model to rate the severity of an antivirus alert on a scale of 1 to 10.
quotes.for: Example of a rating question.

quotes.text: According to Google, the model is nearly five times cheaper than its entry-level Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite LLM.
quotes.for: Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite described as Google's entry-level language model.

quotes.text: The first such model, Jev, was launched in mid-September by a startup called TypeSafe AI Inc.
quotes.for: First decision model: Jev, by TypeSafe AI, mid-September.

quotes.text: Google checked how Gemini Decision 1 compares to Jev and OpenAI Group PBC’s Decisions API, a competing service that launched last month.
quotes.for: OpenAI's Decisions API launched last month; Google ran the comparison.

quotes.text: The search giant says that its model performed better across seven of the nine benchmarks it tested. However, Jev proved to be slightly more cost-efficient.
quotes.for: Seven of nine benchmarks; Jev slightly more cost-efficient.

title: Google joins the decision-model wave with Gemini Decision 1, scoring 1,000 questions in a single pass

quotes.text: After the startup Jev introduced its version, OpenAI, Cloudflare, and Microsoft quickly followed with similar offerings.
quotes.for: Cloudflare and Microsoft also released similar offerings.

quotes.text: Google says it already uses the API internally for dynamic model routing in Gemini Notebook, design prototyping in Stitch, and safety checks in Google Search.
quotes.for: Internal use at Google.

quotes.text: It generates zero text tokens, so output token usage is always 0.
quotes.for: The model generates no output tokens.

quotes.text: Every question runs against the shared input in one forward pass. Questions can't see each other
quotes.for: Questions are scored independently in one pass.

quotes.text: The Decisions API doesn't support context caching, Batch API, or Flex or Priority inference.
quotes.for: No context caching (the sentence goes on to the Batch API).

quotes.text: Available on the Gemini Developer API (v1beta) with
quotes.for: Availability limited to the Gemini Developer API v1beta.
